_comment: Single registry for every scraper. The three grouped workflows
(scrape_api.yml / scrape_html.yml / scrape_browser.yml) build their GitHub
Actions matrix from this file, so adding a source is ONE line here instead of
a 40-line job block in scrape.yml.
group: how the data is fetched -- api (JSON/REST/XML endpoints), html (markup
parsed from pages), browser (a real Chrome via seleniumbase/undetected).
Grouping matters because each technique wants a different timeout and a
different cron slot: API sources are cheap and can run often, HTML sources are
polite-limited by page fetches, browser sources need minutes of startup.
timeout: per-job timeout-minutes, lifted from scrape.yml where the job
persisted hundreds of rows over the WAN (see the glints comment there).
max_env: the env var that caps rows in one run (each scraper's Settings has its
own env prefix). Leave null when the source has no cap. Only used when a
workflow_dispatch input supplies max_jobs -- normal scheduled runs use the
code defaults.
enabled: false keeps a source out of the matrix until it is deliberately
switched on (Indeed is here because it drives a real Chrome and gets blocked).
browser: true when the source renders pages with Playwright instead of
parsing the markup that plain HTTP returns. The workflow then runs
`playwright install --with-deps chromium` before the scraper, which costs
~40s of download, so only sources that need it pay for it. The binary is
then cached by setup-uv and reused across runs.

himalayas.app/jobs/api - free key-free JSON API; remote-job aggregator spanning many employers rather than one country's board, and one of the few free feeds reporting salary bounds, salary period, seniority and categories. OFFSET pagination (page is ignored); the API caps limit at 20. Category-focused to technical roles. Added 2026-10-12.

jobicy.com/api/v2/remote-jobs - free key-free JSON API; remote jobs with geo, industry, seniority level and contract type. No pagination (page is rejected with HTTP 400), so a run is one request filtered by tag/geo. Added 2026-10-12.

themuse.com/api/public/jobs - free key-free JSON API; ~20,000 pages of company-authored postings, so the largest untapped source measured. Rich company objects, levels, categories and locations. Page-based pagination. Added 2026-10-12.

Timeout raised 45 -> 75 on 2026-10-20 and the run budget cut from 1000 postings to 25, after a full CI sweep failed on this source and nothing else ('The action has timed out after 45 minutes' -- exactly this source's cap, which the workflow passes to timeout-minutes). The budget was the real cause, not the timeout: the CI scrape step passes no row cap of its own unless its max_jobs input is set, so the scraper's own max_jobs_per_run default applies, and 1000 postings over this source's 29 search terms is 58 listing pages plus hundreds of detail requests. The step was killed with the postings fetched but NOT yet persisted, so the run contributed nothing -- Canada's jobbank rows were 40 while the budget said 1000. Measured after the change: 25 postings fetched, parsed, cleaned and persisted in 2 minutes.

data.usajobs.gov/api/search - US federal government board, the single largest US employer by headcount. Needs a free data.gov key, supplied to CI as the USAJOBS_API_KEY repository secret and passed to the scrape step in scrape_api.yml (enabled 2026-10-15, once both were true - a secret that exists but is not wired to the step is indistinguishable from no secret, which is the bug the REED_API_KEY comment above it describes). Locally use USAJOBS_API_KEY or USAJOBS_API_KEY_FILE. ONE search request plus ONE job page per posting: there is no position detail endpoint (/api/v2/position/{id} and four other spellings all 404) and PositionFormattedDescription is a marker object, not text, so the full duties/requirements only exist on the public page. data.gov meters keys at 500 requests/hour, which is what USAJOBS_INTER_REQUEST_DELAY_SECONDS exists to protect - do not lower it without measuring the key's real ceiling. Richest structured fields of any source: pay grade, job series, salary band with interval code, and structured city/state on every posting. Added 2026-10-14.

wellfound.com - startup/tech job board, and the best salary source in the corpus: 6 of 6 postings sampled carried an explicit minValue/maxValue in a named currency with a period. No key, no proxy, no captcha. Discovery works ONLY through /location/<country> and /role/l/<role>/<country>: /jobs returns HTTP 200, renders a page=N pager, and then IGNORES it (pages 1-11 each returned the identical 43 job ids and 0 new ones, measured 2026-10-14), so walking it would burn the request budget re-reading page 1 while appearing to progress. The working paths yield 45-58 distinct jobs per page, 540 distinct US jobs over 11 pages. Listing pages are 600-860KB and detail pages ~100KB, so the page cap is the request-budget knob; timeout 60 because these are the largest HTML pages of any source. /location/canada 404s and is therefore not in the default listing set. Added 2026-10-14.

builtin.com - US tech/startup board; pairs with wellfound to cover the segment the corpus had none of. US-only in practice (every posting sampled carried applicantLocationRequirements name='USA'). Rich: 2-6k char descriptions, posting AND closing dates, and up to 46 benefits per posting; baseSalary on ~3/4. TRAP: the JobPosting node is nested under '@graph' in an ~8.8KB JSON-LD document, so a parser reading json['@type'] finds NOTHING and reports an empty board on a site serving every field - the first probe hit exactly this. Also: geo is a sibling of address on the Place node (not a child), industry is a list on 21/24 postings and a string on 3, jobLocation is a bare dict on 19/24 and a list on 5, and hiringOrganization.logo is an ImageObject dict. Discovery paginates on /jobs?page=N (182 distinct links over 8 pages, 20-27 per page, pager to 1000); robots.txt disallows /search/ and /jobs*?search= so keyword search is off limits, while Allow: /jobs*?page= permits the pagination. Listing pages are 230-400KB. Added 2026-10-15.

careers24.com - South Africa; sub-Saharan Africa had ZERO postings in the corpus before this. No key, no registration, no proxy, which puts it in the buildable set while linkedin/glassdoor/monster/jooble/careerjet are not. THIRD schema.org variant: identifier is a PropertyValue (as wellfound/builtin), JSON-LD is top-level (as wellfound, NOT builtins @graph), and baseSalary nests the figure ONE LEVEL DEEPER than either sibling - {currency: ZAR, value: {@type: QuantitativeValue, value: '180', unitText: 'DAY'}} - with NO minValue/maxValue anywhere. A band-only parser reads None for both bounds and does it SILENTLY: the first implementation of this scraper did exactly that and recorded a salary for 0 of the 40 postings while 15 of them publish one (measured 2026-10-16, re-verified by replaying the old logic against live pages). Nothing errored - salary is optional so the batch validated 40/40 - the coverage just read zero. Measured over 40 postings: baseSalary on 15 (37%), periods yearly 10 / monthly 3 / daily 1, and one with unitText:'' (R 80) which the cleaner DROPS rather than defaulting to yearly, since R 80 is a rate and storing it as annual would be wrong by three orders of magnitude. PARSING TRAP: detail hrefs carry a rank query string (/jobs/adverts/2393633-production-manager-/?jobindex=3), so a regex anchored on the closing quote after the slug matches ZERO adverts on a board that is plainly serving them - careers24 briefly looked empty during triage because of this. Another: a province-only advert puts the province in addressLocality, so a naive join emits 'Gauteng, Gauteng'. COMPLIANCE: robots.txt is real text/plain (646b) with ~16 named agent groups (Scrapy, Yandex, Baiduspider, SemrushBot, PetalBot) several with Disallow: / - but NO 'User-agent: *' group, which under RFC 9309 means this crawler is subject to no rule in the file; urllib.robotparser agrees and reports /jobs and /jobs/adverts as fetchable. The naive 'no * group therefore assume blocked' reading would discard the source. Listing yields 10 adverts and paginates for real (54 distinct ids over 6 pages, changing every page - unlike wellfound, which ignores page entirely). Added 2026-10-15, salary shape corrected 2026-10-16.

apna.co - India; India had ZERO postings in the corpus before this, and this is the HIGHEST-COVERAGE SALARY SOURCE in it: baseSalary on 30/30 postings measured, every one a minValue/maxValue band in INR with unitText MONTH. For comparison careers24 is 15/40, builtin ~3/4, and greenhouse/arbeitnow/indeed/weworkremotely store ZERO amounts across 6575/353/168/90 salary rows. It also carries skills - a real list of 0-11 strings on 15/30 - which is the only source here that fills CleanedJob.skills. TRAP: the salary band is nested under value.value.minValue/value.value.maxValue, a FOURTH distinct layout in this codebase (wellfound/builtin put it directly under value; careers24 puts a bare scalar under value.value). A parser written for any of the others reads None for both bounds and says nothing, because salary is optional. Also: identifier.value is a JSON NUMBER not a string; addressCountry is the ISO code 'IN' not a country name; hiringOrganization.logo is a plain URL string (builtin emits an ImageObject); JobPosting is top-level, not @graph. UNIT TRAP: every measured salary is MONTH, so pay_period is monthly and NOT the 'yearly' default the other cleaners use - storing 180000 as annual would overstate every figure in the source 12x with no error raised. VALIDATOR FLOOR: descriptions run 23-4282 chars (mean 835) and 16/30 are under 100, so the usual 100-char 'substantial description' gate would fail over half of a healthy batch; the floor here is 20, just under the measured minimum of 23. KNOWN GAP, not a bug: apna writes 'Bengaluru' where ref.cities holds 'Bangalore', so city_exact will not match on the spelling and those postings resolve to their state or to country-only - that needs a seed variant or alias, not a parser lookup table. robots.txt is real text/plain (160b); the '*' group disallows only /*.infra.apna.co/, an internal host, and /jobs, /job/<city>/<slug>-<id>, /company and /search are all fetchable. Discovery paginates for real: 25 postings/page, 150 distinct paths over 6 pages with 25 new on EVERY page (contrast wellfound, which ignores page, and mustakbil, which serves the same 41 links on every page). Listing pages are ~1.0MB, so the page cap is the request-budget knob. Added 2026-10-16.

mustakbil.com - Pakistan; Pakistan had ZERO postings in the corpus before this. No key, no registration, no proxy. PAGINATION TRAP: /jobs returns 43 ids and /jobs?page=2 is BYTE-IDENTICAL (398,957b both times, same 43 ids, 0 new) - the page parameter is ignored, so no page param is configured. Breadth comes from category paths instead: of 25 plausible slugs measured, only 8 return HTTP 200 with job links and 17 return 404, and those 8 add 80 ids for 123 distinct postings across nine paths (jobs 43; information-technology 20; engineering 20; sales 20; education 20; healthcare 5; pharmacy 4; finance 4; security 2). RATE LIMIT TRAP: the site throttles AT THE CONNECTION LEVEL, not with a 429 - a burst of listing fetches succeeds and then every detail fetch fails with ConnectionError until a multi-minute cool-off. Measured 3.5s between requests was NOT enough; 75s of total quiet restored service, so the default MUSTAKBIL_INTER_REQUEST_DELAY_SECONDS is 4.0 and a run reporting high fetch_failures has this symptom. PAYLOAD: JobPosting top-level; descriptions 2-4k chars carrying real <b>/<ul>/<li> structure; baseSalary is a band nested under value.value.minValue/maxValue with currency PKR and unitText MONTH (the same shape apna uses, different from wellfound/builtin); experienceRequirements is a nested {@type: OccupationalExperienceRequirements, monthsOfExperience: 12} node - the only source here yielding an actual experience figure; addressCountry is the ISO code 'PK'; identifier.value is a STRING (apna's is a JSON number); hiringOrganization.logo is a plain URL string; validThrough carries SEVEN fractional-second digits (2027-01-16T19:00:00.0000000Z) which datetime.fromisoformat rejects before Python 3.11, so the date is read from the leading YYYY-MM-DD by regex; no skills field, so CleanedJob.skills is honestly empty rather than empty because a parser missed something. robots.txt is real text/plain (1882b); the '*' group is Allow: / disallowing only /clearCache, /clearcache and /content/images/ads/, none of which is a job path. pay_period is monthly, not the yearly default the other cleaners use - the one measured salary was PKR 40,000-60,000 MONTH, and PKR 40,000 stored as annual would understate the role by an order of magnitude. Added 2026-10-16.

alfred.is - Iceland; Iceland had ZERO postings in the corpus before this. No key, no registration, no proxy. DISCOVERY TRAP: the homepage embeds a full job feed in __NEXT_DATA__ (props.pageProps.jobs) advertising totalCount 572 / totalPages 22, and it is the WRONG thing to scrape - it serves only 27 records and every pagination attempt returns a BYTE-IDENTICAL 667,028b page with 0 new ids (/?page=2, /?p=2 and /?page=3 are all page 1, because the page is statically generated); /starf?page=2 and /page/2 are 404. robots.txt disallows /api/* and every filter param (*jobtypes=*, *tags=*, *zips=*, *cat=*), so the JSON API - the one route that would have reached the whole feed in a few requests - and the faceted views are unavailable by the site's own rules. What robots DOES nominate is Sitemap: https://alfred.is/sitemap.xml, whose sitemap-jobs.xml child holds 624 /starf/ URLs, so discovery reads the sitemap: compliant, and the only path that reaches the whole board. A crawler trusting the homepage feed would have collected 27 postings and reported success. PAYLOAD: top-level JobPosting, 9 of 10 fields on every posting (title, description, datePosted, validThrough, hiringOrganization, directApply, employmentType) plus jobLocation on 7/10 with addressCountry 'Iceland' (a country NAME, where apna and mustakbil use ISO codes); descriptions 17-2656 chars in Icelandic; logo is a plain URL string. TWO ABSENCES THAT ARE FACTS ABOUT THE BOARD, NOT PARSER GAPS: no identifier at all (0/10) so the URL slug is the only stable key, and no baseSalary at all (0/10) so every row has salary_disclosed=False and NO pay_period is claimed about a figure that does not exist - the only source in the corpus where that is true. validThrough is nullable in the source, and jobLocation is absent on 3/10, so a country-only row is a real outcome. GENERAL-APPLICATION PAGES: a few sitemap entries are not vacancies (e.g. /starf/almenn-umsokn-1 carries 591 chars describing the employer's business, not a role); they are dropped before validation and counted as general_application_dropped in the run summary rather than silently shrinking the batch. Postings are in Icelandic; core.jobs.language_code plus the existing translation kernel is the right place to handle that, and nothing is translated at scrape time. robots.txt is real text/plain (157b) with the '*' group at Allow: /* - only /api/* and the four filter params are disallowed, none of which this scraper requests. Detail pages are 240-250KB, among the largest served here, so the page cap is the request-budget knob. Added 2026-10-16.

net-empregos.com - Portugal; Portugal had ZERO postings in the corpus before this. No key, no registration, no proxy. DISCOVERY: /jobs yields 18 ids and ?page=2 gives 18 NEW ones, so the pager is real (unlike wellfound, which ignores page). Detail URLs are /jobs/<id>/<slug>/ with a 6-12 digit id. JSON-LD TRAP: the JobPosting block is MALFORMED -- the description string contains raw newlines, which makes json.loads raise Invalid control character, so a strict parser reads NOTHING from every page (which is what the first probe reported). The fix is json.loads(block, strict=False), which tolerates control characters inside strings; every field extracts cleanly that way. PAYLOAD: 8 of 8 fields on every posting measured (title, description, datePosted, validThrough, employmentType, hiringOrganization with name+logo, jobLocation with full address, industry); addressCountry is the ISO code 'PT'; descriptions 3400+ chars in Portuguese; employmentType FULL_TIME. TWO ABSENCES THAT ARE FACTS ABOUT THE BOARD: no identifier at all (0/3) so the URL id is the only stable key, and no baseSalary (0/3) so every row has salary_disclosed=False and NO pay_period is claimed about a figure that does not exist -- one of only two sources in the corpus where that is true (the other is alfred). robots.txt returns HTTP 406 as text/html, which is not a real robots file, so under RFC 9309 there is no restriction to parse; /jobs and /jobs/<id>/<slug>/ are both fetchable. Postings are in Portuguese; core.jobs.language_code plus the existing translation kernel is the right place to handle that. Added 2026-10-17. CI-BLOCKED: the site returns HTTP 200 with 0 job links to GitHub Actions Azure datacenter IPs (measured 2026-10-17). The scraper works locally (30/30 inserted) but cannot run in CI without a residential proxy. Same class as the Cloudflare boards.

careerjunction.co.za - South Africa; the country's second-largest board, adding a different employer base beyond careers24. No key, no registration, no proxy. DISCOVERY: /jobs returns 25 links shaped /<slug>-job-<id>.aspx and the pager is IGNORED - ?page=2 returns the same 25 links, so exactly one page is walked (CAREERJUNCTION_MAX_PAGES defaults to 1). JSON-LD TRAP: the JobPosting block is MALFORMED - the description string contains raw newlines and HTML entities, which makes json.loads raise Invalid control character, so a strict parser reads NOTHING from every page. The fix is json.loads(block, strict=False). PAYLOAD: title, url, datePosted, validThrough, description, industry, employmentType, baseSalary, hiringOrganization (name+url), jobLocation (address with locality+country, geo lat/lon); addressCountry is the ISO code 'ZA'; descriptions 3400+ chars in English. THREE TRAPS THAT ARE FACTS ABOUT THE BOARD, NOT PARSER GAPS: (1) no identifier, so the URL id is the only stable key; (2) baseSalary is present but its value is the string 'R Undisclosed', which is not a salary - so salary_disclosed is always False and no pay_period is claimed about a figure that does not exist; (3) employmentType is 'Default', which is not a schema.org value and deliberately maps to employment_type_code NULL. DATES: datePosted/validThrough are formatted '2026/10/16 10:33:33 AM', not ISO 8601, so a stdlib date parser returns nothing for every posting. EXPIRED LINKS ARE NORMAL: 2 of the first 25 detail pages were expired postings with no JSON-LD, so validation min_expected_jobs is 20, not 25. robots.txt is real text/plain, 128 bytes: the governing 'User-agent: *' group is 'Allow: /' and disallows only /myprofile/applied-jobs and /myprofile/EditProfile. Registered 2026-10-17. Added to sources.json 2026-10-18 after PR #26 shipped it unscheduled.

vagas.com.br - Brazil; Brazil had ZERO postings in the corpus before this (one of the largest general boards in the country). No key, no registration, no proxy. DISCOVERY: /vagas-de-emprego/ returns 40 links shaped /vagas/v<id>/<slug> and the pager is REAL - ?page=2 returned 40 new ids with zero overlap against page 1. ?pagina=2 also paginates; ?p=2 serves a 30KB page with 0 postings, so it is not the parameter. THREE TRAPS, each measured 2026-10-18: (1) addressCountry is the NAME 'Brasil', not the ISO code 'BR' - every other country-carrying source here emits an ISO code (PT, ZA) and geographic_resolution matches on ISO codes, so an unmapped 'Brasil' resolves to NO country and the row silently collapses onto the global-remote location; the cleaner normalizes it. (2) identifier is a PropertyValue whose 'value' is an INT (2831966), so str() is mandatory - the URL id matches it on 3 of 3 postings. (3) baseSalary nests unitText/minValue/maxValue FLAT under value - a SIXTH distinct layout in this codebase, alongside Wellfound (value.minValue), Careers24 (value.value scalar), Apna and Mustakbil (value.value.minValue band) and Alfred (none) - and a parser written for any of the others reads None and stores a salary of 0 without complaining. It is present on only 1 of 3 measured postings, so salary coverage is partial BY NATURE of the board. unitText is 'MONTH', so pay_period is monthly rather than the yearly default every other cleaner uses: storing a monthly figure as annual would overstate it twelvefold. ALSO MEASURED: no employmentType and no industry at all (0 of 3), so employment_type_code is honestly None; jobBenefits is a comma-separated STRING ('Vale-refeicao, Assistencia medica, Vale-transporte'), not an array; datePosted/validThrough are plain ISO dates; descriptions run 970-2834 chars in Portuguese, each opening with a literal 'Descricao:' label glued to the first word (stripped in the parser); addressLocality and addressRegion are both populated. The JSON-LD block is MALFORMED on some pages (raw control characters), so the parser attempts a strict json.loads first and falls back to strict=False. robots.txt is real text/plain, 689 bytes: the User-agent:* group disallows /auth/, /move_to, /servicos/, /v1/, /api/, /social/, /users/, /token/, /vagas/pesquisas, /suporte, /mapa-de-carreiras/cargo/ and /suporte-flix; the listing and /vagas/v<id>/<slug> are NOT disallowed and a Sitemap is nominated. Registered 2026-10-18. Re-enabled 2026-10-26 after live verification: dedicated scraper fetches /vagas-de-emprego/ clean.

angolaemprego.com - Angola; Angola had ZERO postings in the corpus before this. No key, no registration, no proxy. THE TRAP THAT COSTS THE WHOLE BATCH: employmentType arrives as a LIST (['FULL_TIME']), not the bare string every other source here emits. A cleaner written for them calls value.strip(), raises AttributeError, and because clean_jobs catches per record it drops EVERY posting in the batch while the run still reports success - a silent total loss. Both shapes are accepted. SECOND TRAP: identifier is a PropertyValue whose 'value' is a slug string, neither an int nor the numeric URL suffix - some slugs end '-4818' and others do not, so the URL slug is the key and the identifier is recorded alongside it. NO baseSalary on any measured posting (0/2), so salary_disclosed is always False and no pay_period is claimed about a figure that does not exist - the fourth source in the corpus where that is true after Alfred, Net-Empregos and CareerJunction. ALSO MEASURED: datePosted/validThrough are full ISO timestamps WITH a timezone offset ('2026-10-17T08:30:47+00:00'); addressCountry is not consistently present so SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY supplies AO as the fallback, which is what stops rows collapsing onto the global-remote location; descriptions run 700-1300 chars in Portuguese opening with a literal 'Sobre a Vaga' label; hiringOrganization carries a logo URL; the JSON-LD block is malformed on some pages so the parser tries a strict json.loads first and falls back to strict=False. DISCOVERY: /vagas returns 15 links and ?page=2 returns 15 NEW ones, so the pager is real. COMPLIANCE, AND IT IS THE INTERESTING PART: robots.txt is real text/plain, 460 bytes, User-agent:* is 'Allow: /' and disallows /login, /register, /perfil, /planos, /pagamento, /vagas-sugeridas, /linkstorage, /auth/ AND THREE QUERY-PARAMETER SEARCHES ON THE LISTING PATH - 'Disallow: /vagas?q=', 'Disallow: /vagas?location=', 'Disallow: /vagas?category=' plus 'Disallow: /?s='. Those are the site's own duplicate-content rules, and they are why discovery walks ?page=N and never filters by query: '?page=' is NOT among the disallowed parameters, so the pager is compliant. Registered 2026-10-18.

jobinrwanda.com - Rwanda; Rwanda had ZERO postings in the corpus before this. No key, no registration, no proxy. LARGEST SINGLE-COUNTRY WIN MEASURED SO FAR: 199 postings on ONE page. DISCOVERY IS THE HOMEPAGE, NOT A LISTING PATH: /jobs is HTTP 404 and /?page=2 returns 0 new postings, so there is no pager and the whole board is a single request. Hrefs are RELATIVE (measured 199 relative, 0 absolute) and the pattern accepts both spellings because angola_emprego was the opposite way round and a relative-only pattern there matched nothing. THE BOARD PUBLISHES NO STRUCTURED DATA: no schema.org JSON-LD and no og: meta tags, so this is HTML extraction. <title> is '<Job Title> | Job in Rwanda' and there is NO h1 at all on the detail page; the body is .node__content. .field--name-body is site boilerplate ('Click on the APPLY button to send your application documents:') and is removed, because leaving it in would make that sentence the description of every posting. THE TRAP IS ONE OF OMISSION: THE SITE PUBLISHES NO POSTING DATE AT ALL. Six detail pages were inspected: four carry no date and the two that do carry only a DEADLINE, in prose ('The deadline for submission of applications is 19 October 2026 at 5:00 PM', 'Application deadline Sunday 25 October 2026', 'Application Deadline 28 November 2026'). A regex taking the first date on the page would have written a CLOSING date into posting_date on every row that had one, asserting a recency the site never claims - so posted_date is None on every Job in Rwanda row and only a date inside explicit deadline wording is recorded, as closing_date. The matched phrase is kept in raw_payload['deadline_phrase'] so the extraction can be audited. Consequence for analysis: any freshness query must treat this source as UNDATED rather than reading its NULL posting_date as 'unknown'. There is also NO COMPANY FIELD - the employer appears only inside the posting prose ('The Management of RATWA SACCO HUYE informs...'), which is a sentence, not a field, so company_name stays 'Unknown employer' rather than putting unverifiable strings into core.companies. No salary and no location field are published, so SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY supplies RW and salary_disclosed is always False. COMPLIANCE: robots.txt is real text/plain, 1706 bytes; User-agent:* allows / and disallows only /core/, /profiles/ and /README.txt, so job pages are permitted. Registered 2026-10-18.

jobwebghana.com - Ghana; Ghana had ZERO postings in the corpus before this. No key, no registration, no proxy. PAGINATION IS PATH-BASED: /jobs/ carries 22 postings and /jobs/page/2/ adds 13 new ones. A query form (?page=2) must NOT be used because robots.txt contains 'disallow: /*?*' - every query string. Hrefs are ABSOLUTE (measured 20 absolute, 0 relative) so the host prefix in the link pattern is optional; angola_emprego was the same way and a relative-only pattern there matched nothing on a board serving 15 postings a page. STRUCTURED DATA, BUT ONLY ON THE DETAIL PAGE: the listing carries just a BreadcrumbList, which is why an early triage scored this board 'no structured data, HTML extraction needed'. The JobPosting is on each detail page. A board is only proven to lack structured data once a DETAIL page has been probed. Payload (5 measured): title, description (literal \r\n), datePosted with NO timezone ('2026-10-16T12:56:18'), validThrough, employmentType as a BARE STRING 'FULL_TIME', hiringOrganization (name + sameAs), jobLocation (streetAddress, locality, postalCode, region) and baseSalary. No identifier, so the URL slug is the key. THE SALARY IS A SITE-WIDE PLACEHOLDER AND IS REJECTED: 5 of 5 measured postings carry a byte-identical baseSalary of {'currency':'GHS','value':{'value':'1500','minValue':'1500','maxValue':'8000','unitText':'MONTH'}} - across a Chief Executive Officer, a CCTV Controller and an Accounts Clerk. Those roles do not share one salary band, and the redundant 'value' duplicating 'minValue' is the signature of a site template. Storing it would put the same invented 1500-8000 GHS band on EVERY Ghanaian row inside a well-formed schema.org block, so nothing downstream would flag it and every salary statistic over Ghana would be quietly wrong in the most believable direction available: a plausible number, right currency, right period. It is recorded in raw_payload for audit and NOT stored - the same treatment careerjunction's 'R Undisclosed' gets. The guard is falsification-tested: removing it fails 4 tests including an end-to-end 'no cleaned row carries it'. baseSalary here is a SEVENTH distinct layout in this codebase. Registered 2026-10-18.

acbar.org/en/jobs - Afghanistan; Afghanistan had ZERO postings in the corpus. The Afghan Relief and Development Coordination body's job board. No key, no registration, no proxy. DISCOVERY: /en/jobs returns 20 links shaped /en/jobs/details/<id>/<slug> and the pager is REAL - ?page=2 returned 20 NEW ids. /en/site-page/2 is HTTP 404: that is the pagination CHROME, not the pager, and confusing the two is the obvious way to conclude the board does not paginate. Hrefs are ABSOLUTE (measured 20 absolute, 0 relative) so the host prefix in the pattern is optional. NO SCHEMA.ORG DATA: no JSON-LD, no og: meta tags. Everything is a <dl class='acbar-jd__info-table'> of label/value rows (<dt class='acbar-jd__info-term'> + <dd class='acbar-jd__info-desc'>). Measured keys: Type, Location, Category, Published, Nationality, Gender, Salary, Contract Duration, Vacancy Number, No of Job, plus Education and Experience in a SECOND pair shape (acbar-jd__info-text + acbar-jd__info-text-value). The closing date is separate, in .acbar-jd__deadline-label / .acbar-jd__deadline-value. THE TRAP IS CONTAMINATION, NOT SHAPE: .acbar-jd__body is 4680 chars and contains SIX ISO dates belonging to OTHER postings, inside a .acbar-jd__related carousel. The tell was that the same ten dates came back from two DIFFERENT posting pages. A naive 'first date in the body' extraction therefore assigns a deadline from an unrelated job and splices six strangers into the description. The related block is removed before the body text is taken; afterwards ZERO dates remain, and raw_payload['dates_left_in_body'] records that count so the removal is auditable. TWO THINGS THAT LOOK LIKE DATA AND ARE NOT: (1) 'Salary' is PROSE - measured 'As Per Organization', 'As per scale', 'Negotiable' - so nothing is stored and the verbatim string is kept in raw_payload['salary_text']; (2) 'Nationality' is NOT a country - it reads 'Afghan' or 'National' and describes WHO MAY APPLY, not where the job is, so it is preserved verbatim and never used to derive the country (SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY supplies AF). There is also no company field - the employer appears only in body prose ('Company Profile - Peyawray Rubaat Manufacturing Company') - so company_name stays 'Unknown employer'. Type is 'Full Time' with a SPACE where schema.org writes FULL_TIME, which is why the employment map is keyed on the normalised form. COMPLIANCE: robots.txt is 24 bytes, User-agent:* with an empty Disallow:, so the whole site is permitted. Registered 2026-10-18.

jobs.af - Afghanistan; a SECOND independent Afghan board alongside acbar_jobs, with a different employer base and different markup. No key, no registration, no proxy. DISCOVERY IS THE HOMEPAGE: /public/job/page/2 is HTTP 404, /public/job?page=2 adds 0 new, and re-fetching / adds 0 new - there is NO pager, and all 12 postings sit on one page. Hrefs are RELATIVE (measured 12 relative, 0 absolute) and the pattern accepts both spellings because angola_emprego was the opposite way round and a relative-only pattern there matched nothing. TWO TRAPS: (1) addressCountry is the NAME 'Afghanistan', not the ISO code 'AF' - the same shape as vagas_com_br's 'Brasil' and with the same consequence, since geographic_resolution matches on ISO codes and an unmapped name resolves to NO country, silently collapsing the row onto global-remote; the cleaner normalizes it and keeps the raw value in raw_payload['country_raw'] for audit. (2) datePosted carries MILLISECONDS and a TRUNCATED OFFSET - '2026-10-17 10:48:27.175+00', where '+00' has no minutes, so it is NOT ISO 8601; datetime.fromisoformat only became lenient about that in 3.11, so whether it parses depends on the interpreter. The parser therefore takes the leading YYYY-MM-DD by regex and ignores the tail entirely, which also makes a future change to that tail harmless. validThrough is '2026-10-30 00:00:00+00', the same shape without milliseconds. ALSO MEASURED: employmentType is the bare string 'FULL_TIME'; hiringOrganization carries a name and a logo; NO identifier, so the URL slug is the key; NO baseSalary, so no salary is stored. directApply is true but the corpus has no column for it, so it is recorded in raw_payload rather than invented as a schema change. COMPLIANCE: robots.txt is real text/plain, 661 bytes; User-agent:* is 'Allow: /' and disallows only /dashboard, /discover, /talents, /projects and /wallet, so /public/job/ is permitted. Registered 2026-10-18.

Rate limiting hides behind a clean response: after ~60-80 rapid detail requests the site stops serving #__NEXT_DATA__ at all, and a burst of 30 with no delay returned 30 unusable pages -- so the client waits on that selector, treats its absence as a fetch failure, and backs off. The record is #__NEXT_DATA__ -> props.pageProps.job; the page's ld+json block is NOT read because it disagreed with __NEXT_DATA__ on the address of the same posting (47300 vs 47400, different street). props.pageProps.similarJobs is a list of OTHER postings and is never a fallback. job.salary is a display string -- '4000 - 6000' or, on most postings, 'Undisclosed' -- and is never parsed for digits; the figures are in structuredJobData.baseSalary.value with unitText MONTH and currency MYR. Ltd'); the detail h3 is the title alone and the employer is its own <li>.
